neet_phy_u05_t02_1.working: The torque is τ = rF sinθ = 0.5 × 20 × sin30° = 5 N m.

neet_phy_u05_t02_2.working: The torque is τ = r × F. Its z-component is (2)(1) − (3)(4) = −10, so τ = −10k̂ N m.

neet_phy_u05_t02_3.working: The two forces form a couple, and a couple's torque is the same about any point. About a point on one line, only the other force contributes: τ = 10 × 0.3 = 3 N m.

neet_phy_u05_t02_4.working: A force whose line passes through the axis has zero perpendicular distance, so its torque is zero. A is false. R correctly defines torque magnitude as force times perpendicular distance, so R is true.

neet_phy_u05_t02_5.working: Torque is a vector despite having the same dimensions as work, so Statement I is false. A couple's torque does not depend on the reference point, so Statement II is false.
